A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same crosslinguistic GPT-2 study. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; v1's Appendices A–F are retained, with Appendix G added in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual language-modeling experiments, NP perturbation results, classifier results, and appendix replication and tokenization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds minimal-pair generalization outcomes and statistical comparisons.

M1.justification: The described GPT-2 architecture, training procedure, and sentence/NP perturbation algorithms remain unchanged. The new ΔGenScore procedure evaluates trained models; the PDFs do not establish a revision to the learning method.

E1.justification: The corpora, language coverage, BabyLM replication, and five NP orderings are retained. Section 6 adds a minimal-pair sentence-preference/generalization task using the existing four-language NP evaluation data.

E2.justification: Appendix G newly reports Italian shuffle_local_word3 alongside shuffle_local3 (Table 14), and Turkish shuffle_nondeterministic (Table 19), absent from the corresponding reported v1 comparisons. The principal comparison sets and appendix replication variants otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds a substantial evaluation protocol: construct original/perturbed minimal pairs, retain test sentences containing a perturbed NP, evaluate final checkpoints, and compare sentence-preference accuracies through ΔGenScore. The existing training budgets, tokenizers, and perplexity evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a complementary diagnostic of whether typological and harmonic NP-order preferences appear in generalization despite their absence in perplexity. Appendix G additionally examines whether attested/impossible distinctions persist across training checkpoints. The existing NP_RANDOM control, replication, and vocabulary-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three seeds, confidence intervals, correlations, and an Italian Mann–Whitney test. v2 adds systematic Welch tests with Bonferroni adjustments across checkpoints and NP comparisons (Sections 4.2 and 6.1; Appendix G), without reporting increased runs. Appendix G's 'paired' terminology leaves the exact t-test specification unclear.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds generalization results: NNDA/ANND differences are reported positive across all four languages, while other orderings yield mixed signs in Italian and Portuguese. Tables 8–19 add adjusted p-values. Figure 3 also revises English NP perplexities, such as ANND at step 1200 from approximately 71 to 74, without explaining whether these are corrections or reruns. The SVM macro F1 remains 0.75 with SD 0.08.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a formal definition of ΔGenScore and its two indicator-average components in Equation 1, together with interpretations of its limiting values. This is a limited mathematical addition; neither version contains substantial theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes the absence of human-like typological NP-order preferences in perplexity. v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion add the claim that targeted generalization favors attested and possibly harmonic orderings. They also qualify within-language separation of attested and impossible variants, especially later in training.

C2.justification: v2 interprets generalization results as partial human alignment while requesting broader typological validation. Section 6.2 explicitly identifies lower entropy after NP normalization as a confound, and removes v1's REVERSE_FULL/information-density explanation. The limitations additionally acknowledge unchecked corpus noise and uncertainty about other model architectures.

D1.justification: The stated code/data repository location changes from the xiulinyang account to picol-georgetown. Tokenizer specifications, POS-tag mappings, corpus licensing, GPU hardware, and reported training time remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xu et al. (2025) to motivate targeted evaluation and contextualize discrepancies with perplexity, alongside additional cognitive-model critiques. References including Clark et al. (2023) and Hu and Levy (2023) are removed. The central positioning as a multilingual extension of Kallini et al. remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, tokenization rationale, results, and conclusion undergo widespread rewriting beyond insertion of new results. v2 standardizes LM terminology, reframes research questions around learning behavior, separates Section 6's results and discussion, and moves the OPUS30 rank-correlation passage to Appendix A.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel generalization figure and per-language statistical tables, redraws the main plots with revised labels and legends, highlights English local shuffling in Figure 2, and relocates Table 3. Existing appendix plots are retained and renumbered. Figure 3 incorrectly changes the Portuguese panel label to English.

improvement.justification: The complementary generalization test, significance analyses, and explicit entropy confound improve the support and qualification of v1's largely perplexity-based conclusions. These gains are limited by ambiguous t-test terminology, the unsupported assertion that ΔGenScore = 0 implies consistently training-matching preferences, and Figure 3's mislabeled panel.
